Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-year-old woman with 7-day history of fever, sweats, myalgia, and nausea after recent travel to rural Vietnam; being assessed for possible malaria or other infectious etiology.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Daily fever for 7 days with alternating chills/feeling cold, profuse sweating (incl. night sweats), generalized muscle aches, nausea, poor oral intake, fatigue.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, joint swelling, dysuria, urinary frequency. Chronic screen-related headaches unchanged.  
• Past medical history: Chronic mechanical back pain (under physiotherapy); episodic headaches/migraines.  
• Medications: Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented); OTC ibuprofen & paracetamol per recommended doses for fever.  
• Allergies: Seasonal pollen (hay fever); no drug allergies reported.  
• Social / preventive: Works as a nurse; up-to-date vaccinations incl. Hep B. Non-smoker; moderate alcohol; moderate exercise. Recent travel—3-week trip to Vietnam, returned 4 weeks ago; rural trekking, cycling, river/beach exposure. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (specific agent unknown, possibly combination regimen).  
• Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.

Examination:
No physical examination or vitals documented.

Impression:
Fever of unclear origin post–Southeast Asia travel; rule out malaria and other tropical or systemic infections.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day in-clinic assessment and physical examination.  
• Order urgent blood work: thick & thin blood films for malaria; full blood count, inflammatory markers, additional infectious disease panels as indicated.  
• If unable to attend central clinic, patient advised to present to nearest Emergency Department with clinician note outlining recommended tests.  
• Patient advised to refrain from work until evaluation complete.  
• Administrative staff to contact patient; patient to phone provided number within minutes to secure appointment.  
• Follow-up pending exam and test results.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: objective vitals, physical examination findings, comprehensive allergy & medication reconciliation.  
● No documented internal transcript conflicts.  
● Transcript quality good; minor conversational noise, no significant inaudible sections.
